newsitem.title: USA: NYS court says gov can kill planned regs - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS court says gov can kill planned regs - paper.

text.p: A New York State Supreme Court Justice ruled that Gov George Pataki had the authority to veto new regulations, knocking down a challenge by advocacy groups, the Albany Times Union said on Tuesday.
Supreme Court Justice Joseph Teresi said Pataki had acted within his authority when he gave Robert King the power to kill proposed regulations.

King, director of the governor's Office of Regulatory Reform, was charged by Pataki with reviewing new rules, but the Republican governor went well beyond the traditional scope for King's office, the paper said.

In November, 1995, Pataki issued an executive order that requires all agency heads to submit proposed rules to King for his approval. Further, all new regulations must be approved by the secretary to the governor, the governor's counsel, his director of state operations, and the budget director.

Critics challenged the governor's power to delegate such authority to King after he blocked a Health Department proposed rule that would have obliged social services directors in hospitals to hold a master's degree in social work. Several advocacy groups, alarmed that King had second-guessed the health commissioner, filed a lawsuit.
However, in an April 18 decision, the judge found Pataki's executive order "a constitutional exercize of the governor's executive authority," the paper said.
The lead plantiff, Cynthia Rudder, executive director of the Nursing Home Community Coalition of New York State, said told the paper the ruling likely would be appealed.
